name: Tony Visconti
hook: An American who moved to London to produce records and ended up following David Bowie to a studio 150 metres from the Berlin Wall.
blurb: Visconti moved from Brooklyn to London in the late 1960s and began a production partnership with David Bowie that went on, on and off, for decades. He produced 'Young Americans' (1975), Bowie's 'plastic soul' album, and then, with Brian Eno, two of the three Berlin Trilogy albums recorded at Hansa Studios: 'Low' and '"Heroes"' (both 1977). He is one of the clearest examples on this map of a producer whose work with one artist outlasted every genre both of them passed through.

signatureTracks.title: Young Americans (produced for David Bowie)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The 'plastic soul' record, and evidence Visconti and Bowie's partnership predates the Berlin period most associated with it.
